en: The Philippine Declaration of Independence was proclaimed on June 12, 1898, ending exactly 333 years of Spanish colonial rule that began in 1565.
The Philippine Congress is bicameral, consisting of exactly 24 senators and up to 316 district and party-list representatives in the House of Representatives.
National hero Jose Rizal wrote his final poem, Mi Ultimo Adios, which consists of exactly 14 stanzas with four lines each, before his execution.
The Ati-Atihan Festival in Kalibo is celebrated every third Sunday of January, drawing over one million tourists annually to the province of Aklan.
The Philippines has over 180 distinct living languages, but only Filipino and English are designated as the two official languages of the national government.
The indigenous Ifugao people built the Banaue Rice Terraces, which sit at an altitude of 1,500 meters and have been cultivated for over 2,000 years.
The Philippine national flag features a yellow sun with exactly eight rays inside a white triangle, representing the first eight provinces that revolted against Spain.
National scientist Ramon Barba invented a mango flowering technique using potassium nitrate that allows trees to bear fruit year-round instead of just once a year.
During the 2022 national elections, over 67 million registered Filipino voters cast ballots to elect one president, one vice president, and thirteen senators.
The historic Malolos Constitution was drafted and ratified by exactly 211 delegates during the Malolos Congress in 1898, creating the First Philippine Republic.
The National Museum of the Philippines complex in Manila houses over ten thousand cultural artifacts and artworks spread across its three distinct, neighboring government buildings.
The traditional Bayanihan practice originally required a coordinated team of 20 to 30 men to carry an entire nipa hut on bamboo poles.
